title: SOG Busts Fake Medical Degree Racket That Sold MBBS, MD Credentials to Around 300
excerpt: Rajasthan's SOG arrested four people, including a Class 11 dropout police say worked as a junior resident at Safdarjung Hospital — a claim the hospital categorically denies.
body:
• Rajasthan Police's Special Operations Group (SOG) has arrested four people in a multi-state racket that allegedly sold fake MBBS, MD and radiodiagnosis degrees and got them uploaded to university websites so they would pass online verification.
  • ADGP Vishal Bansal said more than 300 people across the country had allegedly obtained fake professional qualifications from the ring, which advertised through a Facebook page and WhatsApp.
  • The central accused, Ramkishore Mahawar, studied only up to Class 11, police say; he allegedly paid about Rs 5.5 lakh for forged Class 12, MBBS and MD certificates and Rs 8.5 lakh in all across the scheme.
  • Police say Mahawar joined Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital as a contractual junior resident in June 2025 — a claim the hospital categorically denies, saying its records show he never worked there in any capacity. A Class 11 dropout who allegedly bought his way into hospital jobs with forged medical degrees is at the centre of a multi-state fake-degree racket busted by Rajasthan Police's Special Operations Group, which says the network supplied fake MBBS, MD and other qualifications to more than 300 people across the country.

The SOG arrested four people: Ramkishore Mahawar, who allegedly used the fake credentials; Satyajit Panigrahi, who allegedly ran the social media advertisements and handled customers and council registrations; Manish Manjhi of Gwalior, who allegedly prepared the forged certificates; and Khurram Taufeeq, who allegedly created backdated degrees and uploaded them to university websites so the qualifications would appear genuine during online verification, according to police accounts reported by Medical Dialogues and others. The arrests were made across states in November, beginning with Mahawar's arrest in Delhi on November 8.

How the racket worked

According to ADGP (SOG) Vishal Bansal, the ring operated through a Facebook page called "Medical Education, New Delhi" and approached customers on WhatsApp. Its division of labour — sales, production, uploads — meant members in different states handled finding customers, forging degrees and marksheets, and planting the records on university websites. Police said fake certificates linked to dozens of universities were found. The case began with a complaint by the Rajasthan Medical Council's registrar at Jaipur's Ashok Nagar police station on October 6, 2024, concerning registrations obtained with forged documents, and was later transferred to the SOG.

"After the accused deposited approximately Rs. 5.5 lakh into a specified bank account, he received the 12th-grade, MBBS, and MD (Gynaecology) certificates via DTDC courier."

— Vishal Bansal, Additional Director General of Police, SOG Rajasthan

From ward boy to 'doctor'

Police gave a detailed account of Mahawar's path. From Karauli in Rajasthan and educated only to Class 11, he worked at a private nursing home in Dausa from 2016 to 2022, then as a medical assistant in Balotra typing ultrasound reports, and at a private hospital in Bayana assisting a gynaecologist. There, police say, he obtained a PDF of an MBBS degree purportedly issued by Rama Medical College in Uttar Pradesh, altered it to carry his own name, and registered with the Rajasthan Medical Council — then worked about 15 days as a doctor at a private hospital in Kharela, Dausa.

Mahawar then moved to Delhi, working as a nursing assistant and ward boy at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital between August 2024 and April 2025, where he came across the Facebook advertisement. For around Rs 6.5 lakh, the ring offered a Class 12 certificate in the name of the Tamil Nadu Education Board, MBBS and MD (Gynaecology) degrees in the name of Sikkim Manipal University, and registration with the Delhi Medical Council. After paying about Rs 5.5 lakh, he received the certificates by courier and secured Delhi Medical Council registration number 33624, police said. He later obtained a Diploma in Medical Radiodiagnosis (DMRD) through the same network, had it added to his registration within days, and began working as an on-call sonographer at hospitals in Delhi. In total he allegedly paid about Rs 8.5 lakh, including a switch to forged Maharashtra University of Health Sciences degrees once he realised his credentials could be verified online.

The disputed Safdarjung claim

One part of the police account is directly disputed. The SOG says Mahawar used the forged documents to join Safdarjung Hospital as a contractual junior resident in June 2025. VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital have categorically denied this, saying its official records show Mahawar never worked at the institution in any capacity, contractual or otherwise, and that the hospital follows prescribed rules with due vigilance in engaging personnel and verifying credentials. Queries to the Delhi Medical Council about Mahawar's registration remained unanswered in the reports.

What happens next

Bansal said the SOG is working to identify other members of the network and, critically, the people who obtained medical council registrations using fake degrees — each of whom may have treated patients. For patients and families, the practical check is the register: a practising doctor's name and registration number can be verified with the state medical council that issued it.
nri_angle: Families in India and abroad rely on hospital credentials being real; the case shows how to verify a doctor's medical council registration before treatment.
author: Diaspora Desk

Ramkishore Mahawar arrested in Delhi; further arrests follow across states through November.
